topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture’s place in the series and introduces its aims without yet developing its substantive arguments.

topics.label: Mutation accumulation and clonal selection
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how successive mutations can confer competitive advantages that drive clonal expansion and cancer evolution.

topics.label: Epigenetic disruption in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: This material examines whether altered transcriptional accessibility can drive tumor development without new mutations.

topics.label: Stemness, cancer stem cells and cell of origin
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics investigate how a cell’s position in a tissue hierarchy affects its capacity to initiate or sustain tumor growth.

topics.label: Inflammation-induced stemness and cancer initiation
topics.groupedBecause: These examples show how inflammatory signals can confer stem-like properties that enable mutation-bearing cells to develop tumors.

topics.label: Microenvironmental support of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This material examines established tumors’ dependence on supportive surrounding cells as a potential therapeutic vulnerability.

topics.label: Single-cell and spatial methods for studying cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how tissue-based molecular approaches reveal cancer evolution and interactions between cells.

topics.label: Converging conditions for malignant evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This synthesis explains malignancy as the convergence of conditions that favor particular clones, extending that account to susceptibility during childhood development.

topics.label: Lecture close and next lecture
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the lecture and announces therapy as the subject of the next session.
